category_title: Middle school students with severe reading disabilities who disengage from traditional tasks
minimal_context: The student is asked to complete a traditional pen-to-paper writing task in his physical binder during a whole-class activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please open your physical binder and use your pen and paper to write a summary of the reading.

STUDENT: (Sits in silence, looking at the blank paper and never asking for assistance.)

TUTOR: What do you think you should write first?

STUDENT: (Shows no desire to participate in the whole-class activity and leaves his pen on the desk.)

TUTOR: You need to try to get some words down on the page.

STUDENT: (Quietly puts his head on his desk and becomes 'invisible' due to his frustration surrounding academics.)

options.A: Prompt the student to squeeze a stress ball instead of putting his head down on the desk.
options.B: Withhold attention from the student when he engages in the problem behavior of putting his head down.
options.C: Prompt the student to walk out and get a drink of water if he feels himself getting frustrated.
options.D: Remove the pen-to-paper component from the task and allow the student to utilize apps on the iPad.
